answer.reasons: This would not go on air as delivered. The scorebug is clean, slim and readable with the short names, and the operator surface covers clock start and stop, interval and full time. The problem is the stress case the brief calls out: long accented French names. The long home name wraps onto two lines with almost no line spacing, so the accent on the 'É' runs into the line above. That is text over text, and it shows in every frame with the long name, including after the live update. otherProblems: Each logo sits on its own tile, and the tiles don't match: the white logo has a near-black tile with a gold border, while the other two have cream tiles with no border. answer.reasons: This is a clean deep-maroon strip with a thin gold top rule. The gold 'SUPPORTED BY' kicker is easy to read, and the three logo tiles have equal gaps and even padding inside the strip. Putting each logo on a tile is a deliberate way to keep the white, black and full-colour marks visible over a bright, busy stage, and they stay readable over the video, light and busy backgrounds. With long values the logos are still centred in their tiles and nothing is clipped or overlapping. The Take, Update and Out all animate cleanly with no broken frames. The tiles' inconsistent colours are a small style point, not something that should keep it off air.

otherProblems: Each partner logo sits on its own plate inside the maroon strip (G-2 to G-7, G-27 to G-30). That reads as three stuck-on boxes rather than logos placed in the design.

The plates don't match: the white logo gets a near-black plate with a gold border, while the black and full-colour logos get borderless cream plates. The square mark's plate is also narrower than the other two (G-2, G-5), so the row looks inconsistent.

The Update of the kicker to its long value (G-17 to G-21) shows no visible change. The settled long-value frames show the same 'SUPPORTED BY', so the stress kicker is never seen.
answer.reasons: There are no basic mistakes. The kicker is readable gold on maroon, nothing is clipped, the strip holds its place on the light and busy grounds, and the Take and Out are clean. The problem is design. Each logo gets its own plate, and the plates are mixed: one dark with a gold border, two cream, one narrower. That makes the row look like three pasted-in tiles rather than one designed sponsor strip. With the long values, the small shields look lost in wide plates. A designer would rework how the logos sit in the strip before it airs.

otherProblems: Each partner logo sits on a plate of its own: a near-black tile with a gold outline for the white logo and cream tiles for the black and full-colour marks (G-2 to G-7, G-28 to G-30). The plates do not match each other and read as boxes stuck onto the strip, not as one sponsor row.

answer.reasons: The maroon strip and the gold kicker are clean and readable over every background, and nothing clips or overlaps. But the visibility problem with the white and black logos is solved by putting each logo on its own mismatched plate (one dark with a gold outline, two cream), which a designer would send back. Logo scale within the tiles is also uneven: the shields float in wide empty tiles while the colour mark nearly fills its smaller one. Clean basics, but the logo treatment keeps it off air as delivered.

basicMistakes.where: The long day/room line breaks after 'AUDITORIUM ÅSA ·' and the rest runs down the right edge of the panel as a two-letter-wide vertical column ('DA / RK / : / A …'), stretching the panel to about 940 px tall
The same vertical letter-column wrap of the long room value, on the light ground
The stress layout breaks the panel: a huge empty dark block fills most of the left side, and the logo floats in the middle of it, far from the event name

otherProblems: The leaf logo sits on its own white rounded square inside the dark panel. That is a logo on a plate of its own, not integrated with the text.

answer.reasons: This doesn't go to air as delivered. With the sample values it's a tidy small panel, and the Take and Out are clean. The panel grows to almost the full frame height, with a large empty dark area and the logo floating in the middle of it. basicMistakes.where: Third field of the info line (the long logo-description value) breaks into a column two characters wide down the right edge of the panel, one or two letters per line, and stretches the panel from y≈72 to y≈940
Same broken two-character column of letters down the right side of the panel on the light ground

Info line 'DAY 2 · AUDITORIUM ÅSA' is cut off at the bottom of the f0 crop

otherProblems: The leaf logo sits on a white rounded square of its own instead of being part of the lockup.

The panel is wider than its text in the sample state, which leaves a gap on the right.
answer.reasons: G would not go on air. With the brief's own values it is a clean, small dark ident in the top-left corner, but the long values break it. The info line doesn't get shortened with an ellipsis. Instead it wraps into a column of letters two characters wide that runs down to the bottom of the frame and turns the ident into a tall, mostly empty slab with the logo floating in the middle. The leaf also sits on its own white square.

otherProblems: With an empty label (G-6, G-7) the red tab shrinks to a narrow block that holds no text. It reads as an accent, not a fault, and the brief fixes the label as CAMPUS anyway.

The longest Finnish item wraps to two lines and the strip grows taller to hold it (G-13, G-25). That is clean, but a two-line ticker is a little unusual and the padding is tighter than on the single-line items.
answer.reasons: This is a clean, readable strip: a red CAMPUS tab with white text on a dark bar, legible over both the video and the light backgrounds. Long items, including the Hämeenkadun/Kauppakorkeakoulunkadun item, are never cut off and never run under the label; the bar wraps them inside its own area. Items cycle on their own (G-13). Pause holds the current item at 10 s (G-19). Resume and Next item move it on with a short fade between items. The Take and Out animations are clean. The operator panel offers skip, pause and resume. Nothing overlaps, clips or is hard to read in any frame.

otherProblems: With the label emptied (G-6, G-7), the red label block shrinks to a small blank red tab. It reads as a brand accent rather than a broken box, but it holds nothing.
Between items the text area is briefly empty (G-28, G-44). This is a normal crossfade gap, but a viewer sees a blank strip for a moment.
The long Finnish item wraps to two lines with 'klo 19' left alone on the second line. The bar grows upward to hold it, which is clean, but the short orphan line is slightly untidy.
answer.reasons: This is a clean, conventional ticker: a red 'CAMPUS' label block on the left, a dark full-width strip, and white sentence-case text that reads well over both the video and the light background. The long item with the Finnish street names wraps to a second line instead of being cut, and the strip and label grow upward together. Nothing is clipped and nothing runs under the label. All three operator actions work in the frames: pause holds the item through 10 s, resume and next both move on with a clean fade, and the ticker cycles on its own. The take and out animations are tidy fades. The only nits are the blank red tab when the label is empty and the short orphan second line, and neither would stop it going to air.

otherProblems: With empty values (G-6, G-7) the CAMPUS label is gone and a bare red square stub is left at the left end of the strip. The brief fixes the label, so this only shows if an operator clears it.
When a long item wraps to two lines, the strip grows upward (G-13, G-25, G-29–31, G-45–46). The text stays inside the strip, but the ticker's height changes from item to item.
answer.reasons: This would go on air. It's a clean, readable ticker: a solid red CAMPUS block and a dark full-width strip with white text, which reads well over both the dark and the light ground. The long Finnish street-name item wraps to a second line inside the strip and never runs under the label or gets cut off. Pause holds the current item through 10 s (G-19). Next item (G-26–31) and both resumes (G-20–25, G-42–47) step to the next story with a short fade between items, and the Take and Out are clean fades. Nothing overlaps, padding is even and the type is big enough for TV. The only weak point is the empty red stub when the label is cleared, which the brief never asks for.

otherProblems: Stress frame footer reads '1,005 1,005 VOTES · VOTING OPEN': the vote count is printed twice, which a viewer reads as a glitch (G-4, G-5).

After Close voting the VOTE NOW badge disappears and leaves an empty band at the top of the panel. The question does not move up and nothing says voting has closed, so the top padding is clearly uneven (G-18, G-19, G-24, G-52).

The winner call is understated: the name turns gold and the other rows dim, but there is no winner label. The winner's percentage also gets smaller than the losers' figures, which looks inconsistent (G-51, G-52).
Dimmed losing percentages in olive on navy are low contrast in the winner state (G-52).
With empty values the panel stays full height, with the question and '0 VOTES' crammed at the top and a large empty navy area below (G-6, G-7).
Calling the winner straight after the Take changes nothing on screen (G-31).
answer.reasons: The live, result and winner states are clean, readable midnight-and-gold panels, and the close Coro/Götaälvens race is shown with percentages. But the stress frame shows a duplicated vote count ('1,005 1,005 VOTES'), and closing voting just removes the badge, leaving a hole at the top of the panel and no closed state. The winner call is also too subtle for a final, with the winner's own percentage shrinking. In the empty state the panel is mostly empty space. Each of these is fixable, but as delivered a director would send it back.

otherProblems: When voting closes, the VOTE NOW badge disappears and nothing replaces it. The result and winner frames (G-19, G-25, G-52) are left with an empty band above the question, so the top padding is much deeper than the sides.
The stress footer in G-4 and G-5 reads '1,005 1,005 VOTES · VOTING OPEN', so the count appears twice.

The dimmed olive percentages in the winner state have fairly low contrast on the navy.
answer.reasons: This is a clean midnight-blue and gold panel in the right half of the frame. The question, choir names and vote count are large and easy to read on both grounds, and the long Swedish and Spanish names fit with room to spare. Close removes the badge, Result counts the percentages up with bars that match them, and Call after Result highlights Götaälvens Kammarkör in gold and dims the others, so all three steps the brief needs work. Nothing overlaps, gets clipped or loses contrast. The weak points are the empty band left behind when the badge goes, the duplicated count in the stress footer and a fairly quiet winner moment. They would bother a designer, but none of them makes the board look broken.

otherProblems: After Close voting (G-18/G-19 onward), the VOTE NOW badge just disappears. That leaves an empty band above the question, the top padding becomes uneven, and nothing on screen says voting is closed.

The dimmed percentages on the losing rows after the winner call are low-contrast grey-gold on navy. They can still be read, but only just.
In the empty-values state (G-6/G-7) the panel keeps its full height with the bottom two-thirds empty.
answer.reasons: G is a clean midnight-blue and gold panel in the right half of the frame. The type is well sized, the bars line up, the long Swedish, English and Spanish names fit without clipping, and the panel reads on both the video and the light background. All three actions work. Close removes the vote-now badge. Result counts up percentages that match the bar lengths. Call, after Result, picks out the winner in gold. Calling the winner straight after the Take changes nothing on screen, but no content is lost. Nothing overlaps, gets cut off or becomes unreadable in any settled frame. The transition frames show only clean wipes and fades. The weak points are design ones: the empty gap left where the badge was, the understated winner call, and the repeated count in the stress footer. None of them breaks the graphic, so I would put it on air.

Celebrate pressed before the result is revealed: nothing changes anywhere on the card (G-20 to G-25 are identical to the settled card).

The cream disc and navy shield clash with the black-and-electric-orange look the brief asks for.

The celebrate step does nothing until the result is shown, and after that it only recolours the name and widens the rule. The empty-value card (G-6) shows only the kicker and a rule, floating at mid-frame.

otherProblems: The winner's crest never appears with the sample values, settled or after any step (G-2, G-3, G-12, G-19, G-52). The card the operator would actually take carries no crest, although the brief asks for it.

Before Reveal result there is a large empty gap between the orange rule and the competition line (G-2, G-12), and the card looks unfinished.

Celebrate, after Reveal result, turns the name orange and widens the rule, which works well. The card still falls short as a winner card. The crest never shows with the sample values. A director would send it back rather than air it.

The faint star-dot pattern behind the text sometimes falls in a letter gap of the kicker and close to the countdown digits (G-43). It is barely visible.
The countdown panel changes width slightly and pulses on Pause and Resume. This is a small motion nit.

The white and gold star logo sits on its own soft glow, centred and in proportion, and stands out clearly on the dark ground. The Swedish title, the English line, the service name and the countdown are all large and easy to read. In every frame, sample and stress values stay inside their bounds, with no collisions or clipping. Pause greys out the digits and Resume picks the countdown up again correctly. The Take and Out are clean fades. The only visible weaknesses are the loose spacing under the one-line long title and the smaller type used to fit the stress values. Neither would stop it airing.

otherProblems: With the long race name (G-4, G-5, G-36), the dim status dot sits alone at the far left of the wide black clock band. About 170 px of empty black separates it from the right-aligned digits, so it looks stranded.

In the compact clock-only layout (G-2, G-13), the dot sits tight against the first digit.

The long Finnish race name wraps to two lines inside its yellow band, nothing is clipped, and the text contrast is strong. The only weak point is the small status dot: it is stranded in empty black in the wide layout and looks murky when stopped. otherProblems: With the long stress values (G-4/G-5, crops G-44/G-45), the English subtitle and the countdown label are cut at a word boundary with no ellipsis ('…welcome to the Christmas', 'BÖRJAR OM · BEGINS IN BÖRJAR OM · BEGINS'). The text stays clean and in bounds, but it reads as unfinished.
In the long-value layout the subtitle shrinks noticeably, and a one-line title leaves a larger gap above the subtitle than the two-line sample does. This is slightly uneven vertical rhythm.
The tiny background star dots sometimes fall in the letter spacing of the tracked service-name line (G-43). A viewer is very unlikely to notice.
answer.reasons: This is a calm, centred, full-frame holding screen in deep blue and candle-gold, and it fits the brief. The white-and-gold star logo shows clearly on the dark ground, and the gold rule sits cleanly between the service name and the title. The serif bilingual title and the large countdown are easy to read on a television. The countdown panel is evenly padded. The clock counts down, Pause dims and holds it, and Resume continues it. Take and Out are clean dissolves. The long values stay inside the frame and the panel, with nothing overlapping or clipped mid-letter. The only visible weakness is that two stress values are shortened without an ellipsis. That is a small refinement issue and not a reason to keep it off air.

otherProblems: In the stress frames (G-4/G-5) and after the title Update (G-26–G-30), the title drops to one line but keeps its two-line height. That leaves a visibly loose gap between the title and the English line.
With long values, the English line shrinks to a fairly small italic (about 24 px high). It is still readable, but it is the weakest text on the screen.
In the empty frames (G-6/G-7), the short gold rule under the logo stays on screen with no service name above it. It is a minor orphan.

Long stress values seem to be trimmed at a word boundary with no ellipsis (the label ends in 'BEGINS', the English line ends in 'Christmas'). The trim is clean, but a viewer might not see that text is missing.
answer.reasons: This airs as delivered: a calm, centred full-frame holding screen in deep blue and candle-gold. The white-and-gold star logo is clear on the dark ground, the bilingual hierarchy reads cleanly, and the countdown is large. No text overlaps, gets clipped or loses contrast in any frame, including the stress frames, whose long service name and label stay inside their bounds. The clock counts down, Pause greys the digits and holds them, Resume restarts it, and the Take and Out animations are clean. The leftover issues are small spacing points that a viewer would hardly notice: the gap after a one-line title, the small English line with long values, and the orphaned rule when fields are empty.

otherProblems: In the long-name layout (G-4, G-5, G-36), the status dot sits at the far left of the black clock band, about 180 px from the right-aligned digits. When the clock is stopped it is a dim olive smudge, so it reads as loose rather than as part of the clock.

The long race name wraps onto two lines with a lot of empty yellow to its right. This is acceptable, but the top band looks heavier than it needs to.
answer.reasons: This is a clean top-right race clock in yellow and black. Its large, heavy MM:SS digits would be easy to read on a phone, and it holds up on both the dark and light backgrounds. The long race name wraps inside its yellow band without being cut off or overlapping anything, and the Update brings it in smoothly. Start counts up and blinks the running dot, Stop holds the time, Reset returns to 00:00, and the Take and Out animations are clean. The operator surface offers all three actions the brief needs. The only design nit is the dim status dot floating far from the digits in the wider layout, and a viewer would hardly notice it.

otherProblems: The sample-value frames (G-2, G-3) look the same as the empty-value frames: only the clock shows and there is no race name. The title band only appears once a race name is filled in (G-4, G-32 to G-36). If the brief's sample really had a race name, that name is not shown.

When the clock is stopped, the lamp is a murky olive dot. It's a little dull next to the clean yellow and black.
answer.reasons: This airs. It's a clean yellow-and-black clock in the top right with large bold digits that are easy to read on a phone, on both the dark and the light backgrounds. In the stress frames, the long Finnish race name wraps to two lines and stays well inside its yellow band, with nothing clipped or overlapping. Start, stop and reset all work in the frames: the clock counts up after Start, holds at 00:01 after Stop and returns to 00:00 after Reset. The Take, Update and Out transitions are clean. The flaws a viewer could notice are small: the race name is missing from the sample frames, and the lamp dot floats a bit apart from the digits in the long layout.
